cards.text: Last time, Abram chased down four kings to rescue his nephew Lot. Then he wouldn't take so much as a sandal strap from the king of Sodom. After these events, the word of the LORD comes to Abram in a vision, and God opens with, "Do not be afraid, Abram."

cards.question: God tells Abram not to be afraid. What does God say He is to Abram?

answers.text: His shield and very great reward

cards.text: Abram answers God with a question of his own: what can You give me? Friend, God just said "very great reward," and Abram's got a follow-up. I respect a man who reads the fine print.

cards.question: Abram asks God what He can give him. What does Abram say he still doesn't have?

cards.text: As things stand, the heir of Abram's house is Eliezer of Damascus. That's who gets it all when Abram is gone.

cards.question: Abram says God has given him no offspring, so a ___ in his household will be his heir.

cards.text: Then the word of the LORD comes to Abram again. And God has an answer about Eliezer.

cards.question: God tells Abram that Eliezer of Damascus will be his heir after all.

cards.text: God says Abram's heir will be one who comes from his own body. Then the LORD takes Abram outside and tells him to look up at the heavens.

cards.question: Out under the night sky, God tells Abram to count the ___ if he is able. Then God says his ___ will be like that.
Abram has no children, and God just promised him offspring like the stars. What does Abram do?

cards.text: "Abram believed the LORD, and it was credited to him as righteousness." Abram gets a sky FULL of stars as a promise, and me? I spent years in a junk drawer counting dust as it fell. Same hobby, friend. VERY different view.
Then the LORD tells Abram, "I am the LORD, who brought you out of Ur of the Chaldeans…" God's reminding Abram where this whole journey started.

cards.question: God says He brought Abram out of Ur of the Chaldeans to give him this ___ to possess.

cards.text: Abram has a question about that land. And friend, I can't judge. When an angel showed up at my drawer, the first thing I asked was if he had the right drawer.

cards.question: What does Abram ask the Lord GOD about the land?

answers.text: How he can know he will possess it
How far its borders will reach
When his family should move there

cards.text: The LORD answers, "Bring Me a heifer, a goat, and a ram, each three years old, along with a turtledove and a young pigeon." Abram asks ONE question and gets back a whole LIST, ages included!

cards.question: Abram brings all of them to God. What does he do with the heifer, the goat and the ram?

answers.text: Splits each one down the middle
Burns each one on an altar
Ties each one beside his tent

cards.question: Abram cuts the turtledove and the young pigeon in half too.

cards.text: Then the birds of prey come down on the carcasses. Abram's got company, and it's the uninvited kind.

cards.question: Abram lets the birds of prey have the carcasses.

cards.text: Now it gets heavy. "As the sun was setting, Abram fell into a deep sleep, and suddenly great terror and darkness overwhelmed him."
Then the LORD says to Abram, "Know for certain that your descendants will be strangers in a land that is not their own, and they will be enslaved and mistreated…"

cards.question: God tells Abram his descendants will be enslaved and mistreated in a land that isn't theirs. For how long?
God says He will judge the nation that Abram's descendants serve as slaves.
After God judges that nation, how do Abram's descendants leave it?
God tells Abram he will live to see his descendants come back to this land.

cards.text: Instead, God says Abram will go to his fathers in peace and be buried at a ripe old age. Peace AND a ripe old age? Friend, I'd frame that promise and hang it right over the oven.

cards.question: God says Abram's descendants will return here in the fourth generation. Why not sooner?

answers.text: The Amorites' iniquity is not yet complete
The land still needs time to rest
Abram's family is not yet big enough

cards.text: When the sun had set and darkness had fallen, something appears. Remember those split animals, with the halves laid opposite each other?

cards.question: In the dark, a smoking ___ and a flaming ___ appear and pass between the halves of the carcasses.

cards.text: On that day the LORD made a covenant with Abram: "To your descendants I have given this land…" All that bird shooing, and THIS is what comes next. Somebody get Abram a chair!

cards.question: God says the land runs from the river of ___ to the great River ___.

cards.text: Then God names the ten peoples whose land it is, from the Kenites to the Jebusites, and yes, the Amorites are on the list. That's where we leave Abram for now, friend, but this story is FAR from done.

findings.problem: The opening card tells events from Genesis 14: Abram chasing down the four kings to rescue Lot, and refusing even a sandal strap from the king of Sodom. The card cites only Genesis 15:1, so those outside facts have no reference.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: This is Eliezer of Damascus's first appearance, and the card never says who he is. Card 6 asks the baker to supply that he is a servant in Abram's household, so the fix needs to rework card 6 as well. Card 6 could ask something else, or Eliezer could be introduced after it.

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: "Out under the night sky" adds a time that Genesis 15:5 doesn't give. Verse 12 later says the sun was only then setting, so the added time may even conflict with the text.

rule.text: Times stay true. No time in the text means none added.

findings.problem: The question asks only about the heifer, the goat and the ram. Leaving out the birds signals that they were handled differently, which gives away the answer to the next card, card 7 (whether the birds were cut in half).

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: The right answer, "The Amorites' iniquity is not yet complete," uses Bible wording ("iniquity") and names a specific people. The wrong answers are plain and generic, so the right answer stands out.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: The fill in the blank asks the baker to guess the exact words of the line ("smoking ___" and "flaming ___"). Nothing told earlier lets the baker reason out firepot and torch over cloud, sword or pillar.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: Most of this stop's choice cards are discovery questions the baker can't reason out from earlier cards: the four hundred years (card 3), leaving with many possessions (card 5), the Amorites' iniquity (card 8), the firepot and torch (card 10), and the river of Egypt and the Euphrates (card 12). More of them need story-card context, or the stop needs different questions.

rule.text: A few discovery questions are fine. Some moments can't be reasoned out, like where Jonah's ship is headed. A few of those are okay, as long as most choice cards are informed guesses.
